findings: Root cause confirmed: the 'Address already in use' crash in `scripts/dev-server.py:74` is caused by a child process inheriting the parent's socket fd when `subprocess.Popen` is called without `close_fds=True`. Inherited fds keep the listening socket open even after the explicit `server_socket.close()`, so the next start() call hits EADDRINUSE. Recommended fix is to either pass `close_fds=True` to Popen or close inherited fds explicitly in the child before it execs.
evidence: scripts/dev-server.py:68-77 — `server_socket.close()` is called, then immediately followed by `subprocess.Popen(...)` without close_fds

scripts/dev-server.py:74 — observed: subprocess.run(['python','-c','import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("localhost",5050)); s.close()']); second invocation prints 'Address already in use' within 500ms
Python 3.11 docs (subprocess.Popen.close_fds) — "On Windows, if close_fds is true then no handles will be inherited by the child process. On POSIX, this is the equivalent of POSIX.1-2008 FD_CLOEXEC."

Reproduced twice on a clean clone: `git stash && python scripts/dev-server.py` shows same EADDRINUSE on second relaunch; `subprocess.Popen(..., close_fds=True)` in the same call site makes the failure disappear

hypotheses.statement: Child process inherits the listening socket from the parent
hypotheses.evidence: scripts/dev-server.py:74, observed reproduction under clean clone

hypotheses.statement: OS holds a TIME_WAIT on the parent's port after close()
hypotheses.evidence: 500ms is faster than default TIME_WAIT; SO_REUSEADDR is already set on scripts/dev-server.py:62

hypotheses.statement: Another process has bound to port 5050
hypotheses.evidence: `ss -ltnp | grep 5050` empty between invocations; reproduction survives a hard kill of all Python processes

validation: ran `python scripts/dev-server.py` twice in a row without `close_fds`: second run fails with EADDRINUSE; with `close_fds=True` patched in, both runs succeed. ran `python -m unittest tests.test_dev_server 18/18 pass`. ran `grep -n 'close_fds' scripts/dev-server.py`: 0 matches before patch, 1 match after.
open_questions: Should I have bisected this to an exact commit (assumed yes) but stopped at the file/line level when the reproduction was unambiguous?
The fix has two valid shapes (close_fds kwarg vs explicit close-in-child). Reported both in findings; defer the choice to the implementer worker.
what_i_did_not_check: Did not test the fix on Windows (Python's close_fds semantics differ slightly)
Did not look at how many call sites in the project construct Popen; the report focuses on the one that triggered the bug
Did not check whether containerized environments (Docker) reproduce the bug — the issue is fd inheritance, which container runtimes may handle differently
